boundary: Structure only. No polling observation is stored or published. A polling-measurement layer requires an explicit owner-approved amendment of docs/political-data/political_source_policy.md and verified reuse rights for each publisher. Polls are never a source for election results, party identity or seats; that rule is unchanged.
purpose: Record documented party-level polling measurements as published by a polling organisation, as measurements with their own method and uncertainty — separate from election results.
proposed_store: polling_measurements (one row per poll × party or electoral list)

fields.poll_id: pl-<cc>-<publisher slug>-<fieldwork end date>; opaque, never reused
fields.commissioner: who commissioned the poll, if published; else null
fields.fieldwork_start: ISO date or null if not published
fields.fieldwork_end: ISO date or null if not published
fields.target_population: as published (e.g. all adults, eligible voters, decided voters); never harmonised
fields.sample_size: integer or null if not published
fields.survey_method: as published (e.g. telephone, online panel, face-to-face); null if not published
fields.list_label_as_published: party or electoral list label exactly as the publisher gives it; no mapping to an Atlas party is implied
fields.reported_support_percent: number as published; never recomputed, rescaled or pooled
fields.base_of_percent: what the percentage is of, as published (e.g. decided voters); required
fields.uncertainty_as_published: margin of error or interval text if published; else null
fields.question_wording_reference: URL or citation if published; else null
fields.source_url: publisher's own page for the poll
fields.raw_snapshot_sha256: hash of the archived publisher page or file
fields.reuse_terms: licence or permission reference; a row without verified reuse rights is not stored
fields.provenance: same provenance object as the election stores

never: infer individual political preferences or any person-level attribute
calculate election-winning probabilities, seat projections or forecasts
generate, smooth, average or pool polling estimates across organisations, populations or methods
treat a poll as an election result or use it to decide party identity
map a published list label to a continuous party series without the identity review used for election data
present two polls with different bases or target populations as one series
presentation_rules: always show organisation, fieldwork dates, base of the percentage, sample size and published uncertainty next to a value
show polls in a section separate from election results
state when a difference between two polls lies inside the published uncertainty
owner_decisions_required: amend the political source policy to permit a polling-measurement layer
approve publishers one by one after reuse-rights verification
decide whether the existing poll-related Event Library record may link to this layer
